title: SES Water's network-wide AI leak alarms cut leak run times by up to 40%
summary: SES Water's Aquasuite Burst compares data from 1,000 flow and pressure sensors with predicted levels and raises leak alarms within minutes; the utility reports that run times fell by up to 40%.
account: Sutton and East Surrey (SES) Water supplies 160 million liters a day to 300,000 homes and businesses in parts of Surrey, Kent and South London. Haskoning states in an undated case study that, before the system, an analyst checked deviations in pressure and flow data by eye once a day. Haskoning says that a trial preceded the rollout across SES Water's whole supply area. The case study identifies the software as Aquasuite Burst, and it describes predictive flow-and-pressure models that alert a 24-hour control room. On 11 March 2024 the BBC (Yvette Austin) reported that SES Water was among the first companies in the United Kingdom using AI across its whole network to reduce leaks. Its 1,000 underground sensors monitor flow and pressure. The technology predicts what levels should be. When a leak happens, the system raises an alarm within minutes and engineers are deployed. Innovation manager Jeremy Heath said that pipes are often repaired before customers notice a drop in pressure. Head of asset strategy Liam Ahearne said that the smart network had reduced leakage run rate times by up to 40%. In the case study, Sian Evans of SES Water says that the tool cut the run time of critical burst mains by 40%. Haskoning attributes the 40% run-time reduction specifically to critical burst mains. The BBC noted the regulator Ofwat's figure that about a fifth of water put into the network in England and Wales is lost to leakage. It gave SES Water's 2022/23 loss of 76 liters per property per day. It cited the Angling Trust's criticism that the company's targets were not good enough. The sources include no regulator's report of a specific repaired burst.
purpose: The smart network detects leaks early by comparing sensor data with predicted levels, so that SES Water can send engineers to repair them sooner. Shorter leak run times are the intended result.
system: SES Water smart network using Aquasuite Burst predictive leak detection, with flow and pressure sensors
taxonomy_note: The measured quantity is leak run time; the water saved is inferred, and Trustible's description names water consumption.

ratings.reason: SES Water reports that leak run times fell by up to 40%, and Haskoning ties the 40% figure to critical burst mains. Both figures come from the utility and its vendor.
No source reports a measured volume of water saved or a leakage reduction attributed to the alarms.

ai_role.statement: Aquasuite Burst compares predicted flow and pressure with live network measurements and alerts SES Water’s 24-hour control room to anomalies. Staff investigate and arrange repairs. Haskoning and the utility report shorter leak run times, but do not isolate AI’s contribution from sensors, response staffing, and other network changes.
